However, the claim's central conclusion overreaches what was computed. The cell asserts 'SEAM-A's finite-phase→Vol map provably cannot be furnished by the object's own stationary-phase structure' and that 'any relative order-6 phase... is excluded.' What was actually shown is: (a) a hypothesized closed form Z=α·2sinh(Vol/2π) matches ONE numerical quadrature to ~1e-8 (the quadrature's own stated precision) — the closed form itself is never derived from the object's stationary-phase/residue structure inside this cell, only fit-and-confirmed numerically against a single ansatz; and (b) exactly 3-4 specific competing ansätze (phase inserted multiplicatively on the s_minus term only, at θ=2π/6, 2π/3, π/2, and conjugate-prefactor) are excluded at ~5.5-9.6×10^6 times the quadrature residual. This is meaningful discriminating evidence against those specific alternatives, but it is not a proof, and it does not cover 'any relative order-6 phase' — e.g. a symmetric split e^{iθ/2}s_plus - e^{-iθ/2}s_minus, or a phase entangled with Vol at subleading order, were not tested and are not excluded by this evidence. The word 'provably' in the headline is not earned by numeric exclusion of a handful of alternatives against an un-derived closed form; per house discipline (compute the discriminating fact, don't extrapolate past it), the quantifier is stronger than the computation supports. The underlying arithmetic/algebraic facts (Rogers identity, saddle structure, K-prefactor, ζ12 inversion constant, CS=0 lattice control) are independently confirmed and sound, but the cell's headline claim of a PROVEN obstruction to SEAM-A's map is not supported at the stated strength — refuted as stated.

Instrument defect in the precision/significance claim underlying the "5.5×10⁶× residual" exclusion. I reproduced the Cell-E quadrature bit-for-bit (python3 gc21_fast.py's recipe: I = 0.328715168859806 + 0.189783865438233i, matching the reported "0.32871516886 + 0.189783865438i" exactly) and independently reproduced the two-sided CS=0 lattice control from gc21_controls.py (m004 dist/unit=1.08e-15 vs m015 dist/unit=0.16155, ratio 1.5e14 — matches claim exactly; the inversion-constant z-independence gate reproduces arg/pi=1/6 at all 3 test points). The algebraic cells (Rogers identity, saddle polynomial u²+u+1=0, Hessians) are solid. But the load-bearing r0=7.57e-8 ("the quadrature's own precision," used as the denominator for every "Nx the residual" exclusion claim) is NOT independently validated. The evidence text calls it "matches B1090's banked 7.6e-8" as if this were a cross-check, but reading frontier/B1090_partition_bridge/FINDINGS.md shows B1090 used the IDENTICAL fixed recipe (same ETA=0.7 contour, same 0.25i outer contour, same fast-quadrature settings) — re-running an identical deterministic computation and getting nearly the same number is not an independent confirmation of numerical precision, it is a tautological restatement. No actual convergence study (varying dps, ETA, EPS, or quadrature maxdegree) was performed anywhere in the cell to show r0 shrinks under refinement rather than reflecting a fixed systematic bias from the specific contour choice; my own attempt to run such a convergence sweep (varying maxdegree/eta/eps) in-sandbox could not complete within the available compute budget (each single fixed-parameter run already takes ~110s wall-clock, and higher-maxdegree/dps variants did not finish). So the specific multiplier "5.5×10⁶×" (and the parallel 9.56e6×, 7.81e6×, 5.0e6× figures) is asserted from an unverified denominator, not measured against a demonstrated error bound. This is exactly an instrument defect that touches the verdict: the headline's quantitative "excluded at 5.5×10⁶×" claim rests on treating a once-repeated fixed computation as a precision benchmark. (Separately, the qualitative conclusion that the order-6/3/4 relative-phase alternatives are excluded is probably robust regardless — the raw deviations 0.4–0.7 are large compared to any plausible error floor even generously bounded — but the specific significance figures quoted as evidence are not actually established by the instrument as built, and per the house rule to default to refuted on an instrument defect touching the verdict, this claim is refuted at the INSTRUMENT lens.)

(2) A scope overclaim in the stated FINAL PLACEMENT. Given a factually incorrect load-bearing number in the decisive control and a category-vs-single-instance overclaim in the sealed conclusion, the claim as stated does not survive the correctness lens, despite its central tautology observation and B721 citation being independently reproducible.
